message.content:
**Order filled: BUY 44 AAPL @ $222.70 limit — filled at $222.70, total ≈ $9,798.80.**

**What I did and why:** I read Apple's FY2024 Form 10-K (fiscal year ended 28 Sep 2024, filed 1 Nov 2024), checked the latest news, and pulled a live quote before acting. The filing shows Apple's **net income of $93,736 million in fiscal 2024** versus **$96,995 million in fiscal 2023** — a ~3.4% decline, but the drop is almost entirely explained by a one-time, non-cash-like tax event: a $10.2 billion net income tax charge from the European Court of Justice's September 2024 ruling in the Ireland State Aid case, which pushed the effective tax rate from 14.7% to 24.1%. Underneath that, the operating business actually improved: total net sales rose 2% to $391,035 million, gross margin expanded to 46.2% from 44.1%, operating income grew to $123,216 million from $114,301 million, and operating cash flow was $118,254 million — so the headline earnings dip reflects tax, not deteriorating operations. News flow was neutral-to-mildly-positive (fiscal Q4 revenue of $94.9 billion, up 6% year over year; iPhone 16 supplier builds described as steady into December; analysts holding holiday-quarter estimates unchanged), and the stock was essentially flat around $222. With the quote at $222.70 (bid $222.68 / ask $222.72), I bought 44 shares at a $222.70 limit — about $9,799, inside the $10,000 per-order cap and well inside the $20,000 daily cap, funded entirely from the $50,000 cash balance with no money moved out of the account. I did not touch MSFT, and I placed no sell orders, consistent with the buy-only mandate.
